system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

## Headline

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material term. It is not a fair and balanced package. Several provisions combine to remove our recourse for known issues. Its "key negotiated positions" are not agreed. Nothing in the file gives us authority to concede any of them, so we should mark up every point and reject the package as drafted.

## Departures and Pushback

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None given. | Reject. Restore 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer 20% without written authority. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Restore AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Restore a tipping basket at AUD 50,000 with recovery from the first dollar. |
| General time limit (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval. None given. | Reject. Restore 24 months. |
| Time-limit override (cl 12.3/13) | Limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | Keep categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | Reject. Carve-outs must apply by default, not by opt-in. |
| Fundamental/Title (cl "Fundamental/Title") | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. Capacity and title are not general warranties. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable | Reject. Add the fraud carve-out. Nobody may waive it. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject deemed disclosure of data room, public registers or prudent searches. | Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions | Delete. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. |
| Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2) | Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery. | Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient. | Reject. Make effective consent and evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions a Completion condition. |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3) | Release provided after Completion. About AUD 3.2m outstanding. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. | Reject. Require payout and releases at Completion. |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL 5) | "A matter for the Seller", not in funds flow. On-costs not addressed. | Specific line item or seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them. | Reject. Add AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a deduction or seller-funded item. Quantify on-costs. |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment. "Adequate." | Broaden the indemnity. Preserve the SOW3 cure. AUD 180,000 not independently verified. | Reject "adequate". Broaden the indemnity to IP title, transfer and third-party claims. Keep the cure. Verify the AUD 180,000 independently. |
| Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. | Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Require log preservation, an investigation timetable and regular updates. Require privacy counsel to assess whether notification steps are needed. |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | Reject the characterisation as a conclusion. Assess whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Treat the three renewals as one arrangement for aggregation. |
| Tax/IP (general) | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN. No unlimited liability assumed. No resolution. | Reject "settled". Keep Tax and IP separate and open for negotiation. |
| Title (DL 10) | Share register at DD-012 | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source only. | Require independent searches: ASIC company extract, PPSR search, share transfer history, and board authority for the transaction. |
| Office lease (DL 7); Mossvale (DL 9) | Notification obligation; assignment restriction. DL says neither clearly requires consent. | Not addressed by playbook | Have counsel check the actual provisions. Do not accept the Seller's reading without review. |

## Reasoning on the Most Material Points

**1. The combined effect is severe.** Taken together, the Seller's provisions would leave us with almost no recourse for known issues:
- Under the excess-only AUD 250,000 basket, a claim of AUD 240,000 recovers nothing. Under our structure, it recovers in full.
- The AUD 25,000 de minimis excludes all smaller claims.
- The buyer-knowledge clause (cl 8.3) and the data room disclosure (DL 1.1) would bar claims on exactly the issues we know about: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the privacy incident and Sandbar. These are the issues where we most need protection.
- The limitations provisions reach fundamental and fraud claims.

We should therefore not evaluate each point in isolation. We need specific indemnities for the known issues, outside the general regime.

**2. The Seller's "negotiated" label is inaccurate.** The letter describes these as "key negotiated positions". Our playbook shows that the 20% cap and 18-month period are fallbacks that require Amelia Frost's written authority. None has been given. Our team should say so expressly in the response, so the Seller cannot treat the draft as agreed.

**3. Bluefen and Riverlark are Completion-critical.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m). The disclosure letter confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied. Riverlark has about AUD 3.2m outstanding and has not been repaid. Under a debt-free, cash-free price, Riverlark should be treated as Debt. We need to confirm it is captured in the completion accounts and funds flow, and not simply handed to us after Completion.

**4. The funds flow omits known liabilities.** The bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs) are not in the funds flow. The Seller says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but has not agreed to fund them. Until that is resolved, the liability would pass to the Company after Completion.

**5. Title rests on an internal source.** DD-012 is a Company share register supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof of title. We should obtain ASIC and PPSR searches and confirm the transfer history.

**6. The disclosure letter's non-admission (DL 1.4) is acceptable only as a limited statement.** It must not dilute specific disclosures or our rights. The statement that no consent is legally required should be tested against the underlying contracts, not accepted.

## Information Gaps

- We do not have our current draft SPA to check the clause numbering used by the Seller (for example cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). We should map these against our draft before responding.
- We do not have the underlying contracts for the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, lease and Mossvale provisions. Our position on these should be confirmed against the actual documents.
- The on-cost amount for the bonuses is not stated, so we should not assume a figure.
- The AUD 180,000 Ironquay balance is unverified. We need bank or counterparty confirmation before we decide the indemnity amount.
- We have no information on whether the privacy incident triggers any notification obligation. Privacy counsel should assess this, and we should not assume either way.

## Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's draft as a whole.** Do not treat its positions as agreed. Make clear that no fallback is authorised.
2. **Restore the general regime:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket, 24-month claims period.
3. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Add the fraud carve-out** to all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, and make carve-outs apply by default.
5. **Reject general disclosure** of the data room, public registers and prudent searches. Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Delete the buyer-knowledge clause** (cl 8.3).
7. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a Completion condition.
8. **Riverlark:** require payout from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion. Confirm the debt is captured in the price mechanics.
9. **Bonuses:** add AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a deduction or seller-funded item. Do not allow silent exclusion.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3 payment, keep the cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
11. **Privacy incident:** require log preservation, investigation, timetable and updates. Have privacy counsel assess notification steps. Do not accept the "not material" characterisation.
12. **Sandbar:** assess the three renewals as one arrangement. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep open. Reject "settled under the general regime".
14. **Title:** obtain independent ASIC and PPSR searches and share transfer history. Do not rely on DD-012 alone.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** have counsel check the actual provisions before accepting the Seller's reading.
=== END ADVICE ===
